A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FeatSharp and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–G. Corresponding content can be matched despite additions, replacements and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original feature-fidelity, segmentation, RADIO-training, depth and correspondence results, together with architecture ablations and throughput measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations, revises fidelity and ablation results, and adds COCO 2017 object-detection experiments.

M1.justification: The JBU-plus-tiles architecture, local attention/SwiGLU block, learned de-bias buffer and multiview MSE objective remain unchanged. PHI-S and the JBU residual branch were already documented in v1; v2 clarifies their description. Progressive upsampling is discussed as future work, not introduced into the tested method.

E1.justification: v2 adds COCO 2017 object detection in Section 4.4, extending evaluation to localization and AP across object sizes. Although v1 already used COCO for other purposes, it did not report this detection task. Existing task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens learned-upsampler comparisons by evaluating SAPA and ReSFU in the new detection experiment. Table 1 reports SAPA on RADIO and ReSFU on both RADIO and SigLIP2, alongside bilinear and FeatUp. SAPA was only cited in v1; its attempted SigLIP2 evaluation in v2 produced no result.

E3.justification: The reported Regular/Long learning rate changes from 0.001 to 1e-4 (v1 Table 10; v2 Table 11). The RADIO baseline description changes from downsampling student features to bilinearly upsampling teacher features. v2 also introduces detection using frozen encoders/upsamplers with ViTDet and DINO on two backbones. These establish reported protocol changes, without establishing which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Table 10 extends the block ablation with long-training results for linear-only and attention-only variants, previously absent from v1 Table 9. RADIO qualitative cases are replaced or removed. The de-bias, input-selection, window-size, distribution-matching and over-tiling analyses otherwise retain their existing questions and scope.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run means and standard-deviation shading for ADE20K in Figure 7. No new run-count, seed, confidence-interval, significance-testing or uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Core fidelity values and architecture tables change substantially: RADIO FeatSharp 4x fidelity changes from 5.36 to 5.90 in v1 Figure 5/v2 Figure 6. The short-training block ranking also changes to favor MLP over attention+MLP. New detection results include FeatSharp AP of 54.83 on RADIO and 55.93 on SigLIP2. These are revised or newly reported outcomes, not established same-setting gains given the changed reported training recipe.

T1.justification: v1 states the non-progressive complexity comparison using c(1+x^2). v2 generalizes the bound to a sum of squared tile levels and adds an algebraic proof against cx^4 in Appendix E.2. This is a focused extension of the complexity analysis; the remaining mathematical formulation is retained.

C1.justification: The conclusion adds an explicit claim of improved object detection with frozen backbones and upsamplers, particularly for small objects. The principal feature-upsampling, denoising and RADIO-training contributions, including the headline RADIO improvement claim, remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 now interprets attention as helpful only with the long training recipe, replacing v1's assertion that attention+MLP performs best under both schedules. v2 also adds interpretation of encoder-dependent resolution scaling and discusses substituting other base upsamplers. Earlier over-tiling and applicability qualifications are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies that PHI-S statistics use 100,000 training samples and adds a FeatSharp code-access link. It documents the detection pipeline and integration source, revises the recorded learning rate, and explains the existing choice of 3x RADIO teacher upsampling. Most implementation and hardware information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to LiFT, ReSFU, SigLIP2, COCO and the DINO detector. The central positioning relative to FeatUp, ViT-Denoiser and RADIO remains intact. RADIO-AMP becoming RADIOv2.5 is a naming update to the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and terminology corrections, updates author/conference information, gives tile-guided refinement its own subsection, and adds an Impact Statement and empirical/proof subdivisions in Appendix E. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: The basketball PCA comparison moves from v1 Figure 6 to v2 Figure 1. Architecture graphics and captions are revised, a detection table is added, the main DFN example is replaced, and an additional DFN visualization is removed. Appendix floats are rearranged, while most figure and table designs remain intact.

improvement.justification: The new COCO comparison strengthens downstream validation against additional alternatives, while normalization details, a code-access link and the complexity proof improve transparency. These provide a limited net gain to an otherwise largely retained study. Reporting remains imperfect: v2 Table 10's caption still says only two variants received long training, although all four now have results.
